clue.text: Figure of mystery revealing insect swallowing admiral with grunt in a pickle

indicators.note: one piece swallows another, so the jumble goes inside the insect

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: being in a pickle means in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A mysterious figure is revealed as a bug that has gulped down a grunting naval officer in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admiral' suggests a naval rank or the butterfly, but it is only anagram fodder; 'in a pickle' jumbles it with GRUNT, and 'swallowing' lodges the result between the B and the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is an area of the Atlantic famed for unexplained disappearances, a geographical shape steeped in mystery.

clue.text: Tom Waits's preference was to resort to blotto — "oh no" to iffy brain removal (Neanderthal aftermath)

indicators.note: read as re-sort, to sort again, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The singer chose to fall back on drunkenness, dismissing a dodgy operation on the brain as a caveman's legacy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole fodder runs from the second 'to' to 'aftermath', fifty letters rearranged by 'resort' (re-sort); 'was to' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer Tom Waits famously quipped that he would prefer a drink in front of him to having his brain surgically altered.

One dealing in securities is more skint?

definitions.meaning: a stockbroker buys and sells shares and bonds for clients

explanation.definitionFit: A stockbroker trades securities, and jokingly the comparative of broke, meaning penniless, would be one letter longer.

clue.text: See 2
Yul Brynner was holding note in song

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: the actor Yul Brynner was famously bald
la is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The bald film star hums a note during a song.
explanation.walkthrough: Yul Brynner, the shaven-headed star of The King and I, stands for BALD; 'was holding' puts LA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song, often slow and sentimental.

clue.text: See 2
Labour, virtually last, holding a vote about ignoring Tony's leadership

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it
virtually means almost, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to last is to endure

indicators.note: about signals the letters being shuffled around
ignoring means leaving something out of the word vote
the leadership of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political piece about the Labour Party nearly finishing, holding a ballot that ignores Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks political but is the definition. 'virtually' drops the final E; 'ignoring Tony's leadership' leaves VOE, and 'about' shuffles A with it into EAVO, which 'holding' places inside ENDUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Endeavour as a noun means effort or toil, a synonym of labour as hard work.

clue.text: Style of distress signal reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so a word with the same sound is meant

parts.note: a flare is fired as a distress signal at sea

explanation.surface: A question of the style of an emergency signal, as told by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair means stylish talent or panache, a synonym of style.

clue.text: Most base me on a highly constructed fabrication

parts.note: taken as written
a bird's nest is a structure built high up in a tree

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a lowly person has lied about them in an elaborate tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highly constructed fabrication' looks like an elaborate lie but is a bird's nest built high up; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanest means lowest or most ignoble, synonymous with most base.

clue.text: Seat of power for mischief-maker given head transplant

indicators.note: the first letter is swapped for another, here a K

parts.note: a gremlin is an imaginary imp causing mechanical mischief

explanation.surface: A troublemaker's head is replaced so they can take the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The new head letter K is not clued; it is found by the solver from the change of G.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the Moscow citadel that houses the Russian government.

clue.text: Author tricked going left and left again

indicators.note: in an across entry going left means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: to have someone is to trick them, so tricked is had
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A writer was conned, sent leftwards and leftwards once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl was a British children's author of Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.

clue.text: 3 dart about with a further side on these

definitions.text: 3 dart about with a further side on these

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around

parts.note: the numeral three spelt out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geometric musing: three darts around a shape with one more side than three.
explanation.walkthrough: The '3' is the number THREE, not a cross-reference to 3-down; the whole clue also describes the answer, solids with one side more than three.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetrahedra are solids with four triangular faces, one face more than three, hence a further side.

clue.text: Insubstantial pixies, one topless

indicators.note: one of the two loses its first letter

parts.note: pixies are fairies, two of them here
a pixie is a fairy

explanation.surface: Two little sprites, one going without a top, look flimsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pixies' gives two fairies; 'one topless' strips the F from the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy-fairy means vague, fanciful and lacking substance.

clue.text: Twisting peaks of the southwest and Jerusalem

parts.note: tors are rocky hilltops on the moors of south-west England, such as Dartmoor
Sion (Zion) is a name for Jerusalem

explanation.surface: A tour twisting across West Country hills and the holy city.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a rocky peak on the moors of Devon and Cornwall in south-west England; SION is a variant spelling of Zion.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the act of twisting, a noun naming twisting.

clue.text: Fantasy island for all to see accommodated old-timer

indicators.note: the letter is taken into the jumble, lodged inside it
fantasy suggests an imagined version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: An imagined island open to everyone housed an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantasy' rearranges ISLAND into SNDIAL; 'accommodated' puts U inside after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial is an old-fashioned timekeeper, so jokingly an old timer.

clue.text: Comprehensive work of cleaner

definitions.meaning: brushing floors with a broom is a cleaner's task

explanation.surface: A thorough job done by the cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping means wide-ranging, and is also the act of brushing dirt away with a broom.

clue.text: Worship single hunky partner, almost dead, embraced

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single

indicators.note: the outer piece embraces the other inside it

parts.note: dory partners hunky in the phrase hunky-dory

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Someone adores their lone muscular other half, nearly lifeless, in a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunky-dory is an old phrase meaning fine, so the partner of 'hunky' is its second half. 'almost' trims the final E from the word for dead, and 'embraced' sets what is left inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is the worship of idols, so it is worship, especially excessive devotion.

clue.text: Fanciful situation of Welshman (Tory) we abandoned

parts.note: Ivor is a typical Welsh male name

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Welsh Conservative politician's dreamy position that the rest of us have deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like it means left behind, but it signals the shuffle that turns two words into YTOWER; Ivor is a stereotypical Welsh name.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivory tower is a state of privileged seclusion from practical reality, an unrealistic situation.

clue.text: Trip stupid person up in mid-thought

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the middle three letters of thought

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Someone trips a fool up while deep in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the fool upside down to TIN in this down clue, and 'in' puts it inside the central letters of thought.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short excursion, a trip.

clue.text: Position of responsibility no longer pending?

explanation.surface: A job held responsibly that is no longer waiting to be filled.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a position of authority, and read as two words it means taken off ice, no longer held in abeyance.

clue.text: High cost of something dropped

definitions.meaning: costing a ... is British slang for very expensive

explanation.surface: An expensive item falls from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb is British slang for a lot of money and is also an explosive device dropped from planes.

clue.text: See 2
A pint? Absolutely!

definitions.meaning: a pint in a pub is not a half pint

explanation.surface: A drinker is offered a pint and eagerly agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A full pint of beer is not a half, and the British exclamation means very much so.

clue.text: Dessert ingredient about to go wrong sbortly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: an ingredient is a part of a mixture

indicators.note: a misprint for shortly, meaning the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to fail is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A pudding component is on the verge of collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sbortly' is a typo for 'shortly', which trims the last letter, leaving FAI; 'about' wraps the ingredient around those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A parfait is a frozen or layered dessert of cream, fruit and syrup.

clue.text: Misanthrope presents shark to the audience?

indicators.note: said to an audience means heard, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a loan shark lends money, a loaner

explanation.surface: A hermit introduces a predatory fish to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shark' is the money-lending kind, a loaner; 'presents' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A misanthrope shuns people, and a loner keeps to themselves.

clue.text: Fish eating sister (strange problem)

indicators.note: one piece eats the other, so the second goes inside

parts.note: cod is a fish
a nun is a religious sister
rum is British slang for strange

explanation.surface: A fish swallows a nun, which is a puzzling matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange problem' looks like the definition; 'strange' is RUM and 'problem' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A conundrum is a confusing and difficult problem or riddle.
